title: Dynamical Low-Rank Compression of Neural Networks with Robustness under Ad

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The main text gives the bound κ(S) ≤ exp( (1 / (2 σ_r(S))) R(S) ) + c, but the proof in Appendix C derives the bound ln(κ(S)) ≤ (1/(√2 σ_r(S)^2)) R(S), leading to κ(S) ≤ exp( R(S)/(√2 σ_r(S)^2) ). The two expressions are incompatible: the denominator in the main text lacks a square on σ_r(S) and uses a different constant, and the added constant 'c' is never defined or justified. The claimed bound is therefore incorrect.

The authors claim to 'prove analytically—and verify empirically—that our regularizer neither degrades training performance nor reduces clean validation accuracy across a variety of network architectures.' The only analytical result is Proposition 3, which treats a toy least-squares problem with a fixed target M, not actual neural network training. This does not constitute a proof for general network training performance or validation accuracy.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 6 (Adversarial Training experiment) and associated text in Section 6
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The adversarial training experiment compares adversarially trained RobustDLRT with baseline and DLRT models that were trained on clean, non-adversarial data. The text acknowledges this confound: 'baseline and DLRT models were trained on static, clean data without adversarial augmentation, while RobustDLRT was trained with adversarial batches. This difference confounds attribution of performance gains solely to the regularizer.' The comparison is therefore invalid; the observed robustness of RobustDLRT may be due to adversarial training rather than the proposed regularizer.

The title and abstract are truncated: 'Dynamical Low-Rank Compression of Neural Networks with Robustness under Ad'. The full phrase should be 'Adversarial Attacks'. This is an obvious presentational defect that needs correction.
